tasks.subject: Verified per-market grid tariff rates for presets (S18)
tasks.description: Research task, not code: find verified published grid-tariff rates for Norway, Denmark, Germany and the Netherlands that can be encoded as presets, with a source for each. If no defensible source exists for a market, say so instead of inventing figures. Deliverable: a short research note under docs/research/ naming the source, the peak/off-peak windows and the unit per market, plus a recommendation on which markets are safe to ship.
tasks.output:
S18 research complete. Note: docs/research/grid-tariff-presets-2026.md (148 lines, local-only by .gitignore policy — not committed).

Findings by market:
- Norway (Elvia): two-rate day/night fits the model. Day weekdays 06–22 = 46.40 øre/kWh incl. VAT + elavgift/Enova; night weekdays 22–06 and weekends/public holidays = 31.40 øre/kWh; same energy rate tiers 1–5, fixed 150–755 kr/month by daily-max tier. Source: elvia.no "Nettleiepriser for privatkunder" (2026). Calculated pre-tax 28.99/16.99 øre, VAT-only 36.24/21.24 øre. Operator-scoped preset only, conditional on Tibber tax basis; holidays would be overcharged because the app knows only Swedish holidays.
- Denmark (N1): 2026 C-customer tariff is three-tier and seasonal: lav 10.98; høj 16.47 summer / 32.95 winter; spids 42.83 summer / 98.84 winter øre/kWh incl. VAT, windows lav 00–06, høj 06–17 & 21–24, spids 17–21, summer Apr–Sep / winter Oct–Mar, all days; netabonnement 421.84 kr/yr. Cannot be encoded faithfully in a two-rate model (three periods + seasonal peak rate). Sources: n1.dk/gaeldende-priser and n1.dk/elregning.
- Germany: no national grid tariff; 2026 household netzentgelte vary ~2.46–17.39 ct/kWh by DSO. FairNetz official 2026: 8.16 ct/kWh + 70 EUR/yr net; its §14a controllable-load Module 3 is three-tier (NT 2.04, HT 11.87, ST 8.16 ct/kWh with published windows). Westnetz household 9.53 ct/kWh + 80.30 EUR/yr net (secondary; official PDF restricted). Not safe as a national preset; per-DSO flat preset would need operator selection and net→gross conversion.
- Netherlands: small-consumer grid transport is capacity-based at Enexis (3×25 A = 39.65 EUR/month / 475.84 EUR/year incl. VAT, no per-kWh line). Liander explains normal/dal is a supplier tariff (dal weekdays 23–07 + weekends/holidays), not a grid fee. No per-kWh grid transport exists to put in GridTariff; not safe.

Recommendation: ship only Norway/Elvia as an operator-scoped preset after resolving the tax-basis question and documenting the holiday limitation. Do not ship Denmark, Germany or the Netherlands in the current model; a faithful set needs GridTariff model work (three periods or seasonal peak rates, operator identity, tax-basis metadata, capacity-fee alternative). Keep custom entry and the existing "no published rates" notice for those markets. No figures were invented; residual unknowns are listed in the note.
